name: Address size is 32 bytes instead of 20
description: On Solana, "an account address consists of a 32-bytes key, which is represented by the address type. This data model differs from Ethereum 20-bytes addresses."

name: Ethereum hex address literals not supported
description: On Solana, "an address literal has to be specified using the address"36VtvSbE6jVGGQytYWSaDPG7uZphaxEjpJHUUpuUbq4D" syntax." and "Ethereum syntax for addresses 0xE0f5206BBD039e7b0592d8918820024e2a7437b9 is not supported."

name: Balances and values are 64-bit wide
description: "All balances and values on Solana are 64-bit wide, so the builtin functions for address .balance, .transfer() and .send() use 64-bit integers." This differs from Ethereum where values are 256-bit.

name: Function selectors are 8 bytes (discriminators)
description: "Function selectors are eight bytes wide and known as discriminators." On Ethereum, function selectors are 4 bytes.

name: msg.sender not available on Solana
description: "msg.sender is not available on Solana." The documentation explains: "the Solana VM has no mechanism for fetching the caller accounts. This means there is no way to implement msg.sender." The recommended alternative is using authority accounts that must be signers for the transaction.

name: No ecrecover builtin; signatureVerify replaces it
description: "There is no ecrecover() builtin function because Solana does not use the ECDSA algorithm, but there is a signatureVerify() function, which can check ed25519 signatures. As a consequence, it is not possible to recover a signer from a signature."

name: Try-catch statements not supported
description: "Try-catch statements do not work on Solana. If any external call or contract creation fails, the runtime will halt execution and revert the entire transaction." The compiler will raise an error if try-catch usage is detected.

name: Error definitions and reverts with error messages not working
description: "Error definitions and reverts with error messages are not yet working for Solana."

name: Value transfer with function call not permitted
description: "Solana Cross Program Invocation (CPI) does not support this, which means that: Specifying value: on an external call or constructor is not permitted; The payable keyword has no effect; msg.value is not supported."

name: receive() function not permitted
description: "receive() functions are not permitted on the Solana target." The documentation explains: "On Solana, there is no method that implements this. The balance of an account can be credited without any code being executed."

name: Contracts cannot be types on Solana
description: "On Solana, contracts cannot exist as types, so contracts cannot be function parameters, function returns or variables. Contracts on Solana are deployed to a defined address, which is often known during compile time, so there is no need to hold that address as a variable underneath a contract type."

name: Constructor syntax uses ContractName.new() instead of new ContractName()
description: "On Solana, the address is either passed to the call using the {program_id: ...} call argument or is declared above a contract with the @program_id annotation. As the constructor does not return anything and its purpose is only to initialize the data account, the syntax new Contract() is not idiomatic on Solana. Instead, a function new is made available to call the constructor."

name: Sending value to a new contract not available on Solana
description: When creating contracts with an initial value using {value: ...} syntax, the documentation states: "On Solana, this functionality is not available."

name: Salt and gas cannot be set for new contract creation
description: "The gas or salt cannot be set on Solana. However, when creating a contract on Solana, the address of the new account must be set using address:."

name: Calling contracts uses different syntax on Solana
description: "A call to a contract on Solana follows a different syntax than that of Solidity on Ethereum or Polkadot. As contracts cannot be a variable, calling a contract's function follows the syntax Contract.function(). If the contract definition contains the @program_id annotation, the CPI will be directed to the address declared inside the annotation."

name: External calls require accounts to be specified
description: "External calls on Solana require that accounts be specified." When calling an external function or invoking a constructor, "one needs to provide the necessary accounts for the transaction." If {accounts: ...} is missing from an external call in an external function, the compiler auto-generates the AccountMeta array; otherwise, it must be manually created.

name: Gas cannot be set on external calls
description: "The gas cannot be set on Solana for external calls."

name: delegatecall not available on Solana
description: "delegatecall is not available on Solana."

name: gasleft() not available on Solana
description: "gasleft() is not available on Solana. Gasprice is not used on Solana. There is compute budget which may not be exceeded, but there is no charge based on compute units used."

name: blockhash() not available on Solana
description: "This function is not available on Solana." The documentation notes the recent block hashes account is deprecated and does not give any slot or block number.

name: tx.gasprice not available on Solana
description: "tx.gasprice is not available on Solana. gasprice is not used on Solana. There is compute budget which may not be exceeded, but there is no charge based on compute units used."

name: tx.origin not available on Solana
description: "address tx.origin — The address that started this transaction. Not available on Polkadot or Solana."

name: block.number returns slot number not block height
description: "On Solana, block.number gives the slot number rather than the block height. For processing, you want to use the slot rather the block height. Slots include empty blocks, which do not count towards the block height."

name: block.gaslimit not available on Solana
description: block.gaslimit is listed under "Ethereum" block properties and is not available on Solana. On Solana, the compute budget model replaces gas.

name: block.coinbase not available on Solana
description: block.coinbase ("current block miner's address") is listed under "Ethereum" block properties and is not available on Solana.

name: block.difficulty not available on Solana
description: block.difficulty ("current block's difficulty") is listed under "Ethereum" block properties and is not available on Solana.

name: selfdestruct() not available on Solana
description: "This function does not exist on Solana."

name: msg.sig is bytes8 on Solana instead of bytes4
description: "bytes4 (Polkadot) or bytes8 (Solana) msg.sig — Function selector (or discriminator for Solana) from the encoded calldata, e.g. the first four or eight bytes." On Ethereum, it is 4 bytes.

name: indexed event field attribute has no effect
description: "On Solana, the indexed event field attribute has no effect. All event attributes will be encoded as data to be passed for Solana's sol_log_data system call, regardless if the indexed keyword is present or not."

name: No send() and transfer() on address payable
description: "On Solana, there are no transfer and send functions. In order to alter the balance of accounts, one might increment or decrement the lamports field from the AccountInfo struct directly. This is only possible if the accounts whose balance is being changed are owned by the program."

name: Balance checking uses AccountInfo lamports instead of address.balance
description: "On Solana, the balance of an account can be accessed using the lamports member of the AccountInfo struct. Every account whose value we want to check must be declared with an account annotation." This differs from Ethereum's address.balance.

name: ERC-20 interface not compatible with Solana
description: "The ERC-20 interface is not compatible with Solana at the moment."

name: Dual account model: program account and data account
description: "A Solidity contract on Solana utilizes two accounts: a data account and a program account. The program account stores the contract's executable binary and owns the data account, which holds all the storage variables. On Ethereum a single account can store executable code and data."

name: this returns program account, not data account
description: "The keyword this returns the contract's program account, also know as program id." and "On Solana, this returns the program account. If you are looking for the data account, please use tx.accounts.dataAccount.key." On Ethereum, this refers to the single contract account.

name: External function type calls require accounts argument on Solana
description: "On Solana, external calls from variables of type external functions require the accounts call argument. The compiler cannot determine the accounts such a function needs, so it does not automatically generate the AccountsMeta array."

name: Packed encoding uses little endian
description: "Packed encoded uses little endian encoding, as WASM and SBF are little endian virtual machines." This differs from Ethereum's big endian encoding.

name: abi.encodeWithSignature uses different discriminator format on Solana
description: "On Solana, the signature is known as the discriminator image. It is the function name without any arguments, converted to camel case, and preceded by the prefix global:. For example, if you had the function foo_bar(uint64), the discriminator image would be global:fooBar." This is equivalent to abi.encodeWithSelector(bytes8(sha256(bytes("global:fooBar"))), ...) for Solana.

name: Many Yul builtins not available on Solana
description: "Many Yul builtins are not available, as specified in the availability table." The Yul builtins documentation shows that most memory operations (mload, mstore, sload, sstore), call operations (call, callcode, delegatecall, staticcall), contract creation (create, create2), logging (log0-log4), and several others (stop, pop, signextend, selfdestruct, chainid, basefee, etc.) are not available.

name: Clock account required for block properties
description: "Solana requires the clock account to present in the account for the instruction to use any of the block fields." On Ethereum, block properties are available without any special account.

name: address.call() requires accounts argument on Solana
description: "External calls with the call() method on Solana must have the accounts call argument, regardless of the callee function visibility, because the compiler has no information about the caller function to generate the AccountMeta array automatically."

name: @program_id annotation required for contract addressing
description: "When developing contracts for Solana, programs are usually deployed to a well known account. The account can be specified in the source code using an annotation @program_id if it is known beforehand. If you want to call a contract via an external call, either the contract must have a @program_id annotation or the {program_id: ..} call argument must be present." On Ethereum, contract addresses are derived from deployment, not annotations.

name: Account annotations required for functions
description: "For external functions in a contract, one can declare the necessary accounts, using function annotations. @account(myAcc) declares a read only account myAcc, while @mutableAccount(otherAcc) declares a mutable account otherAcc. For signer accounts, the annotations follow the syntax @signer(mySigner) and @mutableSigner(myOtherSigner)." These annotations do not exist in EVM Solidity.

name: Constructor requires @payer annotation for on-chain data account creation
description: "Creating an account needs a payer, so at a minimum the @payer annotation must be specified. If it is missing, then the data account must be created client-side." Additionally, @space, @seed, and @bump annotations may be needed. These annotations are Solana-specific and do not exist in EVM Solidity.

name: Compute budget model replaces gas model
description: "Solana is optimized for low latency and high transaction throughput and has an equivalent concept to gas: compute unit. Every smart contract function is allowed the same quantity of compute units (currently that value is 200k), and every instruction of a contract consumes exactly one compute unit." As a result, "functions for gas are not available on Solidity for Solana."

name: Selector override requires 8-byte arrays on Solana
description: "The given example only works for Polkadot, whose selectors are four bytes wide. On Solana, they are eight bytes wide." When using @selector to override a function selector, the array must contain 8 elements on Solana instead of 4 on Ethereum.

name: msg.value not supported on Solana
description: As part of the value transfer incompatibility, "msg.value is not supported" on Solana. On Ethereum, msg.value returns the amount of wei sent with the transaction.

name: payable keyword has no effect on Solana
description: As part of the value transfer incompatibility, "The payable keyword has no effect" on Solana. On Ethereum, payable is required to allow a function to receive ether.

name: Automatic AccountMeta generation only works in external functions
description: "When there are no call arguments to a constructor call, the compiler will automatically create the AccountMeta array the constructor call needs. Due to the impossibility to track account ordering in private, internal and public functions, such a call argument is only allowed in functions with external visibility." This is a Solana-specific constraint that does not exist on Ethereum.
